The Python template [`analysis-py.qmd`](analysis-py.qmd) has the same
sections, the same figure labels and the same output tables, and produces the
same numbers from the same data.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(purrr)

source("../../shared/R/labtools.R")

RUNS <- c(reference = "data/reference.csv")
```

```{r}
#| label: load
runs <- map(RUNS, read_run)
primary <- runs[["reference"]]
```

```{r}
#| label: banner
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
cat(synthetic_banner(primary$meta))
```

## Data quality

```{r}
#| label: quality
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
for (name in names(runs)) {
  meta <- runs[[name]]$meta
  problems <- validate_meta(meta)
  cat("\n**", name, "** — ", meta$stream_stats$records, " records; ",
      if (length(problems) == 0) "metadata complete"
      else paste0("metadata problems: ", paste(problems, collapse = "; ")),
      "\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-{{IDL}}-something

```

## Uncertainty budget

```{r}
#| label: budget
components <- list(
  list(quantity = "TODO (Paolo)", value = 0, unit = "V",
       distribution = "type-a", std = 0, sensitivity = 1)
)
budget <- budget_table(components, k = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: out-budget
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
cat(budget_to_markdown(budget, caption = "Uncertainty budget",
                       label = "tbl-{{IDL}}-budget"))
```
